decision_reason: A1 gives the low-U_NN pair standing still and sitting and relaxing only one reliable distinction, posture_inclination. The available IMUs do not support a second robust ordinal distinction between these nearly static postures without assuming seat contact, load support, or a fixed leg configuration. For locomotion, A1 separates walking from its nearest seen anchor jogging mainly by overall intensity, while generic rotational_motion and translational_motion conflate physically different regional and directional motions. A2 therefore retains the supported static-posture contrast, splits rotation by trunk versus instrumented distal-limb involvement, splits translation into horizontal and vertical progression, and adds vertical oscillation and movement distribution to provide transferable locomotor and whole-body contrasts. motion_regularity is dropped because every supplied A1 prototype has the same level.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: trunk_rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or gravity-relative orientation-changing motion of the trunk during the activity.

levels.Low: Little or no trunk angular motion.
levels.High: Prominent trunk angular or orientation-changing motion.

attributes.name: limb_rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion in the instrumented distal limbs, comprising the right lower arm and left ankle.

levels.Low: Little or no distal-limb angular motion.

attributes.name: horizontal_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained locomotor progression in the plane perpendicular to gravity.

levels.Low: Little or no sustained horizontal progression.

attributes.name: vertical_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained locomotor progression that changes body elevation relative to gravity.

levels.Low: Little or no sustained change in body elevation.

attributes.name: vertical_oscillation
attributes.definition: Magnitude of repeated up-and-down body excursion along the gravity axis, independently of net vertical progression.

levels.Low: Little or no repeated vertical excursion.

attributes.name: movement_distribution
attributes.definition: Extent to which appreciable dynamic motion is distributed across the trunk and instrumented upper- and lower-limb regions rather than confined to one region.

levels.Low: Motion is negligible or mainly confined to one body region.
levels.Medium: Motion involves multiple regions but remains uneven or limited.
levels.High: Substantial coordinated motion is broadly distributed across body regions.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains a direct, transferable contrast between nearly static postures, moderate walking, and vigorous running, with jogging and climbing stairs providing seen high-motion anchors.
Repetition rate is distinct from motion magnitude and provides a supported contrast between walking and running, with jogging and cycling supplying transferable periodic-motion anchors.
Sustained rapid fluctuation distinguishes smoother static or controlled motions from dynamically rough locomotion without duplicating isolated impact strength.
Short high-magnitude changes provide an impact-specific contrast for running that transfers from jump front & back and remains physically separate from sustained roughness.

Gravity-relative global inclination is the reliable ordinal distinction among standing still, sitting and relaxing, and lying down; lying down supplies the directly relevant seen static-posture anchor.

Variation of the global load-bearing configuration separates stable postures and ordinary level locomotion from activities with substantial posture changes, using lying down and knees bending (crouching) as seen anchors.

Generic rotation conflates trunk reorientation with distal-limb cycling or arm rotation. The chest, lower-arm, and ankle sensors support this regional separation, and the seen activities waist bends forward, frontal elevation of arms, knees bending (crouching), and cycling provide contrasting transfer anchors.

A single translation attribute conflates level progression with sustained elevation change. Gravity-referenced multiaxial motion and velocity proxies support the split, allowing walking and running to share horizontal progression while climbing stairs supplies a vertical-progression anchor.

Although temporal regularity is measurable, every supplied A1 class prototype is High, so the attribute provides no split-specific class contrast and retaining it would add a constant semantic coordinate.

Repeated vertical excursion adds an amplitude-based distinction between walking and faster or airborne locomotion that is not represented by cadence, impacts, or net vertical progression. Jogging and jump front & back provide seen transfer anchors for this weakly covered locomotor distinction.

Multi-location IMUs can distinguish localized limb or trunk motion from coordinated motion spread across the body. This supplies a transferable structural contrast between whole-body locomotion and localized seen exercises without relying on total intensity.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final attributes encode distinct physical factors: motion_intensity measures aggregate energy; cadence measures repetition rate; smoothness measures sustained rapid fluctuation; impulsiveness measures isolated peaks; posture_inclination measures mean global gravity-relative configuration; and posture_variability measures change in that configuration. trunk_rotational_motion and limb_rotational_motion separate regional angular involvement rather than duplicating global posture. horizontal_translation and vertical_translation represent directional sustained progression, whereas vertical_oscillation represents repeated gravity-axis excursion with no requirement for net elevation change. movement_distribution measures the spatial spread of motion across sensor-bearing body regions rather than its magnitude. motion_regularity was removed because it was constant across all supplied prototypes. No additional static standing-versus-sitting attribute was introduced because seat contact, weight support, and a consistent seated leg geometry are not directly guaranteed by the listed IMU capabilities.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
